name: Bahá'í Faith
title: The story of the Bahá’í Faith

text: The Bahá’í Faith began in Iran more than 180 years ago.
In the city of Shiraz, a young merchant said he was the Báb, which means “the Gate”.
src: The Bahá’í Faith arose from the religious ferment of Shi’i Islam in 19th-century Iran / The Báb declares his mission in Shiraz
in Shiraz, a young merchant named Sayyid / declared that he was the Báb, “the Gate”

text: The rulers of Iran met his followers with violence, and the Báb was put to death.
Later, in a garden in Baghdad, Bahá’u’lláh said he was the one the Báb had promised.
src: The clergy and the Qajar state reacted with violence / The Báb himself was executed by a firing squad in Tabriz
he declared to his companions in a garden that he called Ridván / that he was the one whose coming the Báb had foretold

text: Bahá’ís believe in one God, that all humanity is one, and that women and men are equal.
Their Houses of Worship, such as the Lotus Temple in New Delhi, are open to people of all faiths.
src: teaches the oneness of God, of religion and of humanity / the equality of women and men
Bahá’í Houses of Worship, open to people of all faiths / among the best known is the Lotus Temple in New Delhi

text: Today millions of Bahá’ís live in almost every country, and their world centre is in Haifa.
In Iran, where the faith began, Bahá’ís are still treated harshly because of their faith.
src: Estimates range from about five to eight million, in almost every country of the world / with its world centre in Haifa and Acre
Persecuted in Iran from its beginnings to the present day
